briefdescription.para: Header-only helpers for printing the startup banner, configuration and ASCII logo.

detaileddescription.para: This header defines the Banner class, a small set of static functions that print the startup information to the terminal. The functions print a labelled value, a decorative separator line, the project's ASCII-art logo in a random colour, and the logo plus a final flush. Everything lives in the header, so no separate .cpp file or linking step is needed to use it.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This file is the server's "face" at startup. Server::print_banner() calls these helpers to show the effective configuration, version, port, thread count and API documentation address before Drogon begins handling requests. The banner is useful for confirming that environment variables were read correctly and for spotting a wrong port or database setting immediately. Without it the server would still run, but operators would have no quick on-screen summary of which settings took effect.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
Pseudo-random number generation (random_device, mt19937, distributions): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/numeric/random
Raw string literals (R"(...)"): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/string_literal
Variadic templates and parameter packs (Args&&...): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/parameter_pack
The fmt formatting library: https://fmt.dev/latest/index.html
